title: The business case through the project lifecycle
blurb: Trace the business case from outline in starting up, to full in initiation, through each stage boundary, to benefits confirmed during and after the project.
question: A project is about to end its second delivery stage. What should happen to the business case now, and who checks it before the next stage starts?

teach.h: One business case that grows up with the project
teach.body: Formally: the business case is developed in outline and then in full at the beginning of the project, then maintained and checked at each stage, while benefits are confirmed during the project where possible and mostly after it. Develop, check and maintain happen inside the project lifecycle; confirming benefits continues outside it. In plain English: the case starts as a sketch, becomes a detailed argument, is refreshed every stage, and is finally tested against what really happened.

items.label: Develop and check the outline business case
Develop and check the full business case
Maintain; check the updated case each stage end
Update with actuals; confirm benefits so far

teach.h: Where it happens and who decides
head: When
Activity
Business case
Decision
teach.caption: The board also checks the business case when it assesses an exception plan.

teach.body: In starting up, the project mandate is used to prepare a high-level outline business case, which goes into the project brief; the board checks it when authorizing initiation. In initiation, 'prepare the full business case' updates the outline with time and costs from the project plan and the aggregated risks from the project log. The executive is accountable and the project manager responsible. The board approves it when authorizing the project.

During each stage the business case is kept under review, and the project manager checks the impact of issues and risks on it. In managing a stage boundary, 'update the business case' reflects external and project changes, updates the benefits management approach with the results of benefits actions and reassesses aggregated risk; the board checks it before authorizing the next stage. In closing, the case is updated with actual costs and benefits and a forecast of benefits still to come.

teach.h: Each board decision uses the latest version
Inside and outside the project lifecycle
teach.caption: Some benefits are confirmed during the project when products are released iteratively.

teach.body: Northgate Rail Freight is introducing a yard management system. In starting up, project manager Samira Haddad drafts the outline business case for the project brief. In initiation she builds the full case using the project plan's costs and the aggregated risks; executive Owen Pryce is accountable for it. At each stage boundary she updates it with actual spend and new forecasts. At closure the case shows £40,000 of savings already realized, and post-project reviews at 6 and 12 months are planned for the rest.

teach.text: Classic traps: the outline business case belongs to starting up and the full business case to initiation, not the other way round. Post-project benefits reviews are planned inside the project but carried out by the business after closure. And managing a stage boundary is not used at the end of the final stage: closing a project updates the business case instead.

items: Starting up: outline business case (in the project brief); checked at authorize initiation.
Initiating: full business case; executive accountable, PM responsible; approved at authorize the project.
Each stage boundary: 'update the business case'; checked before the next stage.
Closing: updated with actual costs and benefits; post-project reviews planned.
Confirm benefits: during the project where possible, mostly after closure by the business.

summary: You can now trace the business case from outline to full, through each stage boundary and into closure, and say which board decision checks each version. You can also explain why confirming benefits continues after the project while develop, check and maintain happen inside it.

A.q: In which process is the outline business case prepared?
A.why: 'Prepare the outline business case' is an activity in starting up a project (manual 13.4.3).

whyNot.1: Initiating a project prepares the full business case.
whyNot.2: Directing a project is where the board checks it, in authorize initiation.
whyNot.3: Managing a stage boundary updates the existing business case.

A.q: When does the project board approve the full business case?
A.why: The full business case is prepared in initiation and approved by the board when authorizing the project (manual 5.3.1, 14.4.2).

whyNot.0: Authorize initiation reviews the project brief, which holds the outline business case.
whyNot.1: By closure the business case is updated with actuals; approval happened long before.
whyNot.3: Ongoing direction is informal guidance, not approval of the full business case.

A.q: Which activity refreshes the business case near the end of each stage?
A.why: 'Update the business case' is an activity in managing a stage boundary, ready for the board's next stage decision.

whyNot.0: Evaluate stage status is a controlling a stage activity comparing actual with plan.
whyNot.2: The full business case is prepared once, in initiation.
whyNot.3: Report highlights sends a periodic highlight report to the board.

B.q:
Which two statements about the business case lifecycle are correct?
1. The outline business case is prepared in initiating a project.
2. The full business case uses time and costs from the project plan.
3. Post-project benefits reviews are carried out by the project manager before closure.
4. Some benefits may be confirmed during the project when products are released iteratively.
B.why: The full business case is built from the project plan's time and costs and the aggregated risks (2), and some benefits can be confirmed during the project with iterative releases (4).

whyNot.0: Both are false: the outline is prepared in starting up, and post-project reviews happen after closure, run by the business.
whyNot.1: Statement 3 is false: benefits reviews after the project are carried out by the business.
whyNot.3: Statement 1 is false: the outline business case is prepared in starting up a project.

B.q: During a stage, benefit forecasts change but remain within tolerance. Where is this normally reflected?
options: In a new outline business case
In an exception plan prepared at once
In the stage-end business case update
B.why: A change in benefit forecasts is handled in managing a stage boundary, 'update the business case', not by an exception plan.

whyNot.0: The outline business case belongs to starting up; it is not recreated.
whyNot.1: Exception plans respond to forecast breaches of tolerance, which this is not.
whyNot.2: Checkpoint reports cover work package progress from team manager to project manager.

B.q: Who carries out post-project benefits reviews?
options: The project board, in the final stage
B.why: Post-project benefits reviews are planned in the project but carried out by the business after closure; it is not a project activity to undertake them.

whyNot.1: The project manager updates the benefits management approach to plan reviews, but does not carry them out.
whyNot.2: The board ensures reviews are planned when authorizing closure; the business runs them afterwards.
whyNot.3: Team managers deliver products; they do not run benefits reviews.

C.q: In initiation, which information is used to turn the outline business case into the full business case?
options: End stage report results and highlight reports
Project plan time and costs, and aggregated risks
Quality register results and product descriptions
The project mandate and the team plans
C.why: 'Prepare the full business case' updates the outline with time and costs from the project plan and the aggregated risks from the project log (manual 15.4.5).

whyNot.0: End stage reports and highlight reports come after initiation.
whyNot.2: Quality results come from delivery; product descriptions do not supply the costs and risks.
whyNot.3: The mandate fed the outline in starting up; team plans are made in managing product delivery.

C.q: Which pairing correctly matches a board decision to the version of the business case it checks?
options: Authorize initiation: the full business case
Authorize the project: the outline business case
Authorize a stage: the updated business case
Authorize closure: the outline business case
C.why: Before authorizing each further stage the board checks the business case updated at the stage boundary.

whyNot.0: Authorize initiation checks the outline business case in the project brief.
whyNot.1: Authorize the project approves the full business case.
whyNot.3: At closure the business case has been updated with actual costs and benefits.

C.q: Which statement about the business case lifecycle is correct?
options: Maintaining the business case continues after closure
The full business case is first drafted in starting up
The outline business case is replaced in each stage
Confirming benefits continues after the project closes
C.why: Develop, check and maintain happen within the project lifecycle; confirming benefits continues outside it, mostly after closure (fig 5.3).

whyNot.0: Maintaining happens at each stage end inside the project.
whyNot.1: Starting up drafts the outline business case; the full one comes in initiation.
whyNot.2: One business case is maintained and updated; the outline is not replaced each stage.

reteach.title: From sketch to scorecard
reteach.question: How does an architect's idea for a house change from first sketch to the year after the family moves in?

blocks.body: First comes a sketch, enough to decide whether detailed design is worth paying for (outline business case, starting up). Then full drawings and costs before building starts (full business case, initiation). The drawings are revised at each milestone as prices and problems emerge (update at each stage boundary). A year after moving in, the family judges whether the house delivered what they hoped (benefits reviews, after closure).

blocks.text: Outline in starting up, full in initiation. Benefits reviews are planned by the project but run by the business afterwards.

explain.body: The mandate is used to prepare a high-level outline business case. It sits in the project brief, which the board reviews when authorizing initiation.

test.q: Which product holds the outline business case when the board decides whether to authorize initiation?
test.why: The outline business case is part of the project brief, assembled in starting up and reviewed in authorize initiation.

whyNot.1: The PID is assembled later, in initiation, and holds the full business case.
whyNot.2: End stage reports are produced at stage boundaries.
whyNot.3: The project plan is prepared in initiation.

explain.body: 'Prepare the full business case' adds time and costs from the project plan and the aggregated risks. The executive is accountable; the project manager is responsible; project assurance is consulted.

test.q: Who is accountable for the full business case prepared in initiation?
test.why: The executive is accountable for the business case; the project manager is responsible for preparing it.

whyNot.0: The project manager is responsible for preparing it, not accountable.
whyNot.1: The senior user specifies the benefits but does not own the business case.

explain.body: Near the end of each stage (except the final one) the project manager updates the business case so the board can confirm continued justification before authorizing the next stage.

test.q: In which process is the business case updated before the board authorizes the next stage?
test.why: 'Update the business case' is a managing a stage boundary activity.

whyNot.0: Controlling a stage keeps the business case under review but does not run the stage-end update.
whyNot.2: Directing a project is where the board checks it and authorizes the stage.
whyNot.3: Initiating a project prepares the full business case once.

explain.body: In closing, the business case is updated with actual costs and benefits, and the benefits management approach is updated to plan post-project reviews. The business runs those reviews.

test.q: What does the project plan for the period after it closes?
options: Extra highlight reports to the board
test.why: The benefits management approach is updated in closing to plan post-project benefits reviews.

whyNot.0: Delivery stages end when the project closes.
whyNot.1: Initiation belongs to the start of a project.
whyNot.3: Highlight reports stop when the project closes.
